name: Base system
description: Basic packages, time zone, swap memory and automatic security updates.
details:
Waits for apt to be free (on a freshly created server it is usually busy
with updates), installs the given packages, sets the time zone,
creates /swapfile if asked and turns on unattended-upgrades for security patches.

variables.name: base_swap_mb
variables.label: Swap (MB)
variables.help: Swap memory in /swapfile. 0 = do not create. Useful on servers with little RAM.

noUninstall: they are the system's basic packages and settings (time zone, swap, security updates); other programs use them and removing them could break them.

prueba.lab: Yes. In a container the swap is not created (it uses the computer's) and it says so in a note.
pasos: In «Test server», «Create and start» and «Add to Draupnode». Open its page → Modules.
Add «Base system» (Europe/Madrid, default packages) and press «Simulate»: there should be changes and 0 failures.
Press «Apply». Then «Simulate» again.
comprobar: The apply finishes with 0 failures and the second simulation says 0 changes (everything is as requested).
In «Terminal»: «timedatectl» shows Europe/Madrid and «htop --version» responds.
«systemctl status unattended-upgrades» is active (automatic security updates).
necesita: Nothing: it works with the default values. Check the time zone (format Region/City, e.g. Europe/Madrid).
Swap: 2048 MB by default; on servers with little RAM (1 GB) raise it. 0 = do not create.
problemas: It takes long or hangs on «Wait for apt to be free» → a freshly created server is updating itself; wait a few minutes and apply again.
«Swap skipped: the server is a container» → normal on the test server; on a real VPS it is created.

name: Exact time (chrony)
description: Keeps the server's clock exact to the second. It matters for certificates, logs, backups and two-factor authentication (TOTP codes).
details:
Installs chrony (GPL-2.0), the time client of Red Hat, Debian and the
new Ubuntus: it replaces systemd-timesyncd and corrects the time
gradually, without jumps. It uses the given time servers on top of the
ones the system brings.
Optional: changes the server's time zone (empty = leaves it alone).

variables.name: chrony_servers
variables.label: Time servers
variables.help: One per line. The ntp.org «pools» spread the load over many volunteer servers.

uninstallWarning: Removes chrony and leaves systemd-timesyncd (Ubuntu's default) again so the time keeps being adjusted.

prueba.lab: No: inside the test container chrony would change YOUR computer's time (they share the clock). Try it on a virtual machine or a server.
pasos: Add «Exact time» with the default servers and apply.
Change the time servers (for example time.cloudflare.com) and apply again.
comprobar: Server page → Summary → System: the clock shows as synchronised.
In «Terminal»: «chronyc sources» shows the chosen servers, some with «*» or «+».
necesita: Nothing: the default time servers will do.
problemas: «chronyc sources» without any «*» → the provider blocks outgoing traffic on port 123/UDP: use the provider's time server (for example 169.254.169.254 on some clouds).

name: Firewall (iptables)
description: Opens the given TCP ports in the server's firewall and saves the rules so they survive a restart.
details:
Uses iptables + netfilter-persistent, which is what Oracle Cloud's Ubuntu images
come with (their INPUT ends in REJECT, so each port has to be opened).
On Oracle Cloud also open the same ports in the VCN's «Security List»:
that is a separate firewall, outside the server.

variables.name: firewall_tcp_ports
variables.label: Open TCP ports
variables.help: Port 22 (SSH) is always opened even if it is not in the list.

uninstallWarning: Removes the rules Draupnode opened in iptables (except SSH, so as not to lose the connection). The server's other rules are not touched.

prueba.lab: Yes (the test container has iptables).
pasos: Add «Firewall» with ports 22, 80 and 443 and apply.
Then add another port (for example 8080), apply, and then remove it and apply again.
comprobar: Server page → Network and security: «The firewall lets through» shows 22/tcp, 80/tcp and 443/tcp.
In «Terminal»: «sudo iptables -S INPUT» has the rules with the draupnode tag and «/etc/iptables/rules.v4» stores them.
SSH keeps working (the server page is still read) and 8080 appears and disappears when you add and remove it.
necesita: The TCP ports you want open, one per line. The ones other modules need (80/443 for Caddy or nginx, 8000 for Coolify…) are added by themselves when you tick them.
Always keep the SSH one (22 or the one you set in «Secure SSH»): Draupnode does not let you remove it.
problemas: A port opened here cannot be seen from outside → the cloud provider (Oracle, AWS…) has its own firewall: open it in its panel too (the server page warns you if it detects it).

A Docker port can be seen from outside even if it is not in the list → what Docker publishes bypasses iptables; publish apps only on 127.0.0.1 (the modules already do) and go in through Caddy/nginx or the tunnel.

name: Headscale (private network between your devices)
description: A private network between your servers, your laptop and your phone, with the Tailscale apps but with the coordination server at home. Each device connects directly to the others.
details:
Headscale (the free Tailscale coordination server) in Docker.
Unlike WireGuard (everything goes through this server), here devices
talk directly to each other; this server only introduces them. The
clients are the Tailscale apps (also free).
It needs a domain with HTTPS (Caddy or nginx). Draupnode creates the
network user and a key to join devices for 30 days (in “Passwords”):
on each device,
tailscale up --login-server https://your-domain --authkey THE-KEY
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/headscale (included in the backups of the
Backups module). License: BSD-3-Clause.

variables.name: headscale_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: headscale_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Recommended: Tailscale clients want HTTPS (hs.example.com, with Caddy or nginx).

variables.name: headscale_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: headscale_user
variables.label: Network user
variables.help: Devices you join with the key are owned by this user.

variables.name: headscale_base_domain
variables.label: Internal network name
variables.help: Each device will be “name.this” inside the network (MagicDNS). It cannot be your public domain.

variables.name: headscale_update
variables.label: Update Headscale when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

secrets.label: Key to join devices to the network

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Headscale containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (the network, its devices and its keys). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes (without a domain, the client will warn that it is not HTTPS).
pasos: Add “Headscale” (ideally with a domain and Caddy) and apply.
Install Tailscale on your computer and run “tailscale up --login-server <address> --authkey <key from “Passwords”>”.
comprobar: “docker exec dn-headscale headscale nodes list” (in “Terminal”) shows your device.
With two devices joined, one can ping the other's 100.64.x.x IP.
necesita: To use it for real, a domain with HTTPS.
problemas: The key has expired (30 days) → delete /etc/draupnode/secretos/<server>/headscale_clave and apply again.
Devices cannot see each other → they use Tailscale's DERP servers to get out of difficult networks; check they have internet access.

name: Outgoing email (msmtp)
description: Lets the server send emails (cron notices, automatic update notices and program messages) through your email provider's SMTP.
details:
Installs msmtp (GPL-3.0) as the system “sendmail”: whatever the server
sends by email goes out through the SMTP server you set (your email's,
Amazon SES, Stalwart…). Mail to “root” or to any system user reaches the
“Send notices to” address.
If you tick “Automatic update notices”, it writes to you when an
update fails.
The SMTP password stays in /etc/msmtprc, readable only by root:
programs not running as root cannot send email.

variables.name: msmtp_host
variables.label: SMTP server
variables.help: Your email provider's (smtp.example.com).

variables.name: msmtp_port
variables.label: Port
variables.help: 587 (STARTTLS) is the usual one; 465 if your provider uses direct SSL.

variables.name: msmtp_tls
variables.label: Encryption
variables.help: “starttls” for 587; “tls” for 465.

variables.name: msmtp_user
variables.label: SMTP user
variables.help: Usually your email address. Empty = no user.

variables.name: msmtp_password
variables.label: SMTP password
variables.help: Many providers require an “app password” instead of yours.

variables.name: msmtp_from
variables.label: Sender
variables.help: The address emails are sent from (your provider usually requires it to be yours).

variables.name: msmtp_to
variables.label: Send notices to
variables.help: Whatever goes to root (cron, updates, programs) arrives here.

variables.name: msmtp_unattended
variables.label: Automatic update notices
variables.help: It writes to you when an automatic update fails.

variables.name: msmtp_test
variables.label: Send a test email when applying

uninstallWarning: Removes msmtp and its configuration; the server can no longer send email.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add “Outgoing email” with your email's SMTP details and “Send a test email” ticked.
Apply and check your inbox (and the spam folder).
comprobar: The “Prueba de Draupnode” email reaches the “Send notices to” address.
In “Terminal”: “echo hola | mail -s prueba root” reaches you too.
necesita: An email account with SMTP (and its app password, if your provider asks for one).
problemas: “authentication failed” → user or password; Gmail and Outlook need an app password.
“connection timed out” → the server's provider blocks outgoing traffic to that port: try 465 with “tls”.
“sender address rejected” → the sender must be your address on that account.

name: Secure SSH + fail2ban
description: Locks SSH down to the essentials (no root, no passwords, few attempts) and blocks with fail2ban whoever tries passwords.
details:
Writes /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/01-draupnode.conf (it takes precedence over the rest, like
the 50-cloud-init.conf that sets PasswordAuthentication yes) and checks it with
«sshd -t» before reloading: if something is wrong, it leaves it as it was.
So you don't lock yourself out, Draupnode does not let you remove passwords if
it logs in with one, or forbid root if it logs in as root, and when applying it checks
that your user has an authorised key.
fail2ban never blocks the IP you connect from.
If you change the port, it is opened in the Firewall before changing SSH and
Draupnode updates the server at the end. On Oracle Cloud also open it
in the Security List BEFORE applying. Port 22 stays open in the Firewall
until you remove it yourself.

variables.name: ssh_port
variables.label: SSH port
variables.help: 22 is the usual one. Changing it reduces bot noise, it is not real security.

variables.name: ssh_password_auth
variables.label: Allow password login
variables.help: Unticked = SSH key only (recommended).

variables.name: ssh_root_login
variables.label: Log in as root
variables.help: «no» = nobody logs in as root (sudo is used). «solo-con-clave» = root can, but never with a password.

variables.name: ssh_allow_users
variables.label: Only these users can log in
variables.help: One per line. Empty = any user with a key.

variables.name: ssh_fail2ban_bantime
variables.label: Block time
variables.help: Repeat offenders are blocked for a week («recidive» jail).

variables.name: ssh_fail2ban_ignore
variables.label: IPs that are never blocked
variables.help: Besides yours, which is added by itself. One per line (IP or network, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24).

uninstallWarning: Removes the hardening and fail2ban. SSH is NOT uninstalled (it is how Draupnode connects) - it goes back to its previous configuration; if the server came that way, it may accept passwords again.

prueba.lab: Yes. Leave it on port 22 on the test server so as not to lose the connection.
pasos: Add «Secure SSH + fail2ban» with port 22, no passwords and no root, and apply.
From a terminal on your computer, try logging in with a password: «ssh -p 2222 -o PubkeyAuthentication=no ubuntu@127.0.0.1».
comprobar: Draupnode keeps logging in with the key (the server page is read).
The password attempt is rejected («Permission denied (publickey)»).
Server page → Network and security: fail2ban shows as active; in «Terminal», «sudo fail2ban-client status sshd» confirms it.
necesita: Nothing to start: no passwords, no root and fail2ban on.
If you change the port: open it first in the cloud provider's firewall. «Only these users can log in», one per line; empty = anyone with a key.
problemas: After applying nobody logs in with a password → that is expected: log in with your SSH key.
You changed the port and Draupnode no longer connects → the cloud provider has it closed; open it in its panel or go back to 22 from its console.
fail2ban has blocked your own IP → put your IP in «IPs that are never blocked»; meanwhile, log in from another network or wait for the block time (1 h).

name: WireGuard (VPN)
description: Your own VPN. With it you get into the server as if you were on its network, to see panels (Grafana, Cockpit…) without opening them to the internet.
details:
WireGuard (GPL-2) from the system, with the wg0 interface. Each name in
«Devices» (laptop, phone…) has its own configuration: it is generated ON the
server the first time, with its own key, and Draupnode brings it to your
vault. On this module's page you see it with its QR code (for the WireGuard
phone app) or save it as a .conf (for the computer).
Removing a name from the list removes its access.
It opens the chosen UDP port in iptables (if present). On Oracle Cloud open it
also in the Security List, as UDP.
With «All traffic through the VPN», the device goes out to the internet through
the server (useful on public wifi); otherwise, only what is for the server
goes through the VPN.

variables.name: wireguard_peers
variables.label: Devices
variables.help: One per line (laptop, phone…). Each one has its key and its address on the VPN.

variables.name: wireguard_network
variables.label: VPN network
variables.help: A private /24 network not used by your home or the server. The server is the .1.

variables.name: wireguard_endpoint
variables.label: Server's public address
variables.help: The one the devices connect through. Empty = the same one Draupnode logs in with.
variables.patternHelp: IP or name, without a port

variables.name: wireguard_route_all
variables.label: All traffic through the VPN
variables.help: The device goes out to the internet through the server.

variables.name: wireguard_dns
variables.label: DNS for the devices
variables.help: Empty = their usual one. With AdGuard Home on the server it is set by itself (the VPN's .1). Example 9.9.9.9.

uninstallWarning: Stops the VPN and removes the wg0 interface. The devices can no longer connect.
uninstallData: Also delete the server's and the devices' keys (if you reinstall it, they will all have to be configured again).

prueba.lab: Yes: the test container uses your computer's kernel, which has WireGuard. To really connect from a device you need a server reachable from outside (UDP port 51820).
pasos: Add «WireGuard (VPN)» with the devices portatil and movil and apply.
On the module page, «See configurations»: each device's one is there with its QR code.
In «Terminal»: «sudo wg show».
comprobar: wg show shows the wg0 interface with 10.8.0.1 and one peer per device.
On a public server: with the WireGuard phone app and the QR code, you connect and «ping 10.8.0.1» responds.
necesita: The devices, one per line (laptop, phone…): each one will have its configuration and QR code in «See configurations».
UDP port 51820 open in the cloud provider's firewall (Draupnode's only handles TCP).
«Server's public address»: empty = the one Draupnode uses to log in; if you log in through a private IP or a tunnel, set the public one.
problemas: The phone connects but there is no traffic (a «handshake» that never arrives) → 51820/UDP is closed at the cloud provider, or the public address is not the right one.
No internet with the VPN on → «All traffic through the VPN» needs the server to reach the internet; turn it off if you only want to reach the panels.

name: Docker
description: Installs Docker Engine with the official script, leaves it running and gives your user permission.
details:
If «classic storage» is ticked, it turns off the containerd image store
BEFORE any images are downloaded. Without that cAdvisor cannot measure CPU/RAM
per container in Grafana. If Coolify is already installed it is not touched, because
changing it afterwards would leave its containers unable to start.

variables.name: docker_classic_storage
variables.label: Classic overlay2 storage
variables.help: Needed to see CPU/RAM per container in monitoring.

variables.name: docker_users
variables.label: Other users in the docker group
variables.help: Your connection user is always added.

uninstallWarning: Stops and uninstalls Docker. ALL the containers on the server are stopped, including the ones Draupnode did not install.
uninstallData: Also delete /var/lib/docker and /var/lib/containerd (images, containers and volumes of ALL apps). Without this, if you reinstall Docker everything is back.

prueba.lab: Yes (Docker inside Docker, with its data in a separate volume).
pasos: Add «Docker» and apply.
In «Terminal»: «docker run --rm hello-world».
comprobar: The test container says «Hello from Docker!» without using sudo (your user is in the docker group).
The server page shows the Containers tab with its counter and «Clean Docker…».
necesita: Nothing. Your connection user is added to the docker group; add others in «Other users in the docker group».
Leave «Classic overlay2 storage» on if you are going to use Monitoring (otherwise each container's CPU/RAM cannot be seen).
problemas: «permission denied … docker.sock» when using docker in the Terminal → open a new Terminal (the group applies when you log in again).
«no space left on device» → Server page → Containers → «Clean Docker…».

name: Docker image registry
description: Your own private Docker Hub: keep your images on the server and pull them from your computers or your CI with a user and password.
details:
Docker's official registry (CNCF Distribution 3) with a user and
password (generated on the server, in «Passwords»).
To use it from other computers give it a domain (Caddy or nginx) and run
«docker login your-domain»: Docker only talks to registries with HTTPS
(except 127.0.0.1). The images are stored in
/srv/draupnode/apps/registry/data (they can take a lot of space).
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/registry (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: Apache-2.0.

variables.name: registry_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: registry_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: registry_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: registry_user
variables.label: User
variables.help: «docker login» is done with this user and the generated password.

variables.name: registry_update
variables.label: Update the registry when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Docker Registry containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (all the uploaded images). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «Docker image registry» and apply.

In «Terminal»: «sudo docker login 127.0.0.1:5000 -u draupnode» (password in «Passwords»), «sudo docker pull busybox», «sudo docker tag busybox 127.0.0.1:5000/prueba/busybox:1» and «sudo docker push 127.0.0.1:5000/prueba/busybox:1».
comprobar: «docker login» says «Login Succeeded» and the push finishes.
«curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5000/v2/_catalog» without a user returns 401.
necesita: Nothing to test it on the server. To use it from other computers, a domain with Caddy or nginx (Docker requires HTTPS).
problemas: «http: server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client» from another computer → give it a domain (Caddy/nginx) and use «docker login your-domain».
Pushing large images through nginx fails with «413» → raise the maximum request size in nginx.

name: Portainer (Docker panel)
description: A web panel to see and manage Docker: containers, images, volumes, networks, logs and Compose stacks.
details:
Portainer Community Edition (the free one) in Docker. Draupnode creates the
«admin» user with a password generated on the server (in
«Passwords»).
CAREFUL: Portainer handles the whole of Docker, which is equivalent to being root on the
server. Better without a domain: log in with «Open» (SSH tunnel) or through the VPN.
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/portainer (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: zlib (Community edition).

variables.name: portainer_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: portainer_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: portainer_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: portainer_update
variables.label: Update Portainer when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Portainer containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (its configuration, users and saved stacks (your containers are not touched)). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «Portainer» and apply.
Press «Open (SSH tunnel)» and log in with «admin» and the password from «Passwords».
comprobar: The panel shows the «local» environment with the server's containers (the dn-… ones).
From Portainer you can see a container's logs and restart it.
necesita: Nothing: Draupnode creates the «admin» user and its password.
problemas: It asks to create the administrator or says it has timed out → Portainer only reads the password the first time: uninstall it with «also delete the data» and apply again.
It handles the whole of Docker (it is like being root): do not give it a domain unless needed; log in through the tunnel or the VPN.

name: Caddy (web and automatic HTTPS)
description: Publishes your apps on your domain with HTTPS. Caddy requests and renews the Let's Encrypt certificates by itself.
details:
Caddy (Apache-2) from the Ubuntu/Debian repository, as a system service.
Each line in «Sites» is «domain target»:
  photos.example.com 127.0.0.1:2283      → forwards to the app on that port
  blog.example.com /srv/www/blog         → serves that folder (static website)
The domain must already point to this server's IP (A/AAAA record)
and ports 80 and 443 must be open (they are added to the Firewall):
that way Caddy gets the certificate by itself. While the DNS does not point here, that
site will not have HTTPS (the others will). A domain ending in .localhost
uses Caddy's own certificate (for testing).
Before reloading, the configuration is checked: if it has an error, the
previous one keeps running.
It cannot go with Coolify or nginx: all three want ports 80 and 443.

variables.name: caddy_sites
variables.label: Sites
variables.help: One line per site: «domain target». Target = 127.0.0.1:PORT (an app) or /folder (static website).

variables.name: caddy_forward_auth
variables.label: Domains protected with Authelia (set by Draupnode)
variables.help: The ones you choose in the Authelia module. Logging in to Authelia is required before reaching them.

variables.name: caddy_email
variables.label: Email for Let's Encrypt
variables.help: Optional. They warn you if a certificate cannot be renewed.

variables.name: caddy_security_headers
variables.label: Security headers
variables.help: HSTS, not letting the website be framed by another, not guessing file types…

uninstallWarning: Uninstalls Caddy. Your sites can no longer be seen through their domain; the apps behind keep running.
uninstallData: Also delete the certificates Caddy had obtained (/var/lib/caddy). If you reinstall it, it requests them again.

prueba.lab: Yes, but without Let's Encrypt (the test server is not reachable from the internet): use a .localhost domain and Caddy signs its own certificate. With a real domain, the real certificate is tested on a public server.
pasos: First install something that listens, for example «Vaultwarden» (port 8222).
Add «Caddy» with the site «vault.localhost 127.0.0.1:8222» and apply.

In «Terminal»: «curl -sk --resolve vault.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 https://vault.localhost -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}
'».
comprobar: The command returns 200: Caddy serves the app over HTTPS.
Server page → Apps and databases: the site vault.localhost (Caddy) appears.
A second «Apply» changes nothing.
necesita: The sites, one per line: «domain target». Target = 127.0.0.1:PORT (an app) or /folder (static website). App modules with a domain are added by themselves.
For real HTTPS: the domain must point to the server's IP and ports 80 and 443 must be open (also in the provider's firewall). Optional email, for renewal notices.
problemas: The certificate does not come through («obtaining certificate» / «challenge failed») → the domain does not point to this server yet, or 80/443 are closed at the cloud provider.
«Caddy and nginx cannot go together» → choose one of the two.
It answers 502 → the target app is not listening on that port (check it in Apps and databases → Usage per app).

name: Coolify
description: A panel to deploy your apps from GitHub/GitLab with automatic domain and HTTPS (Traefik proxy + Let's Encrypt).
details:
Installs Coolify with its official installer.
If you set an administrator email, Draupnode creates that user when installing with
a password generated on the server itself (stored in
/etc/draupnode/secretos/<project>/coolify_admin, root only). If you leave it empty,
log in STRAIGHT AWAY at http://IP:8000 and create your user: the first one to log in
becomes the administrator (there are 10 minutes).
These two options only count on the first installation; afterwards they are changed
from the Coolify panel.
When ticked, its panel ports (8000, 6001 and 6002) are added to the Firewall
list; remove them from there once the panel has its own domain.
On Oracle Cloud open them in the Security List too.

variables.name: coolify_admin_email
variables.label: Administrator email
variables.help: Empty = the first one to open the panel creates the administrator.

variables.name: coolify_autoupdate
variables.label: Automatic updates
variables.help: Coolify updates itself to each new version. Turn it off if you prefer to update from the panel yourself.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Coolify containers (panel, database, proxy). The apps you deployed with Coolify can no longer be seen through their domain, because their proxy is removed; their containers are not deleted.
uninstallData: Also delete /data/coolify and its volumes (the panel configuration, users, SSH keys and backups). Without this, if you reinstall Coolify everything comes back as it was.

prueba.lab: Yes. It needs 2 GB of RAM and 30 GB of disk; on the test server its panel is at http://127.0.0.1:18000.
pasos: Add «Coolify» (it brings Docker and the Firewall), set your email as administrator and apply (it takes a few minutes).
See the administrator's password on the module page → Passwords.
Open http://127.0.0.1:18000 in your browser.
comprobar: The Coolify panel loads and you log in with your email and that password.
Server page → Apps and databases: «Coolify panel» appears; the apps you publish in Coolify show up there with their address.
necesita: Put your email in «Administrator email»: if you leave it empty, the first one to open the panel (port 8000, open to the internet) takes the administrator account.
At least 2 GB of RAM and 30 GB of disk. It cannot go with Caddy or nginx (all three want ports 80 and 443).
problemas: «1800 MB of RAM needed…» → the server is too small for Coolify.
The panel does not load from outside → open 8000 in the cloud provider's firewall (Draupnode's Firewall already opens it).
«Caddy and Coolify cannot go together» → remove Caddy/nginx: Coolify brings its own proxy (Traefik).

name: Your app (Git or folder)
description: Deploys your app with its docker-compose.yml (for example, the one Docker Creator generates), from a Git repository or from a folder on this computer. When applying, it updates it.
details:
Clones the repository into /srv/draupnode/apps/<name> and starts it with
«docker compose up -d --build». Every time you apply, it fetches the latest from the
branch and builds it again (only what changes is restarted).
Private repository, two ways:
- With the https:// address and a read-only «Access token» (GitHub:
  Fine-grained token with «Contents: Read-only» only for that repository).
  It is stored encrypted in your vault; it is not left written on the server.
- With the SSH address (git@github.com:user/repo.git): Draupnode creates a
  «deploy key» on the server; you see it in «Passwords» and add it to your
  GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo (Settings → Deploy keys, read-only).
Variables (.env): the normal ones, one per line «KEY=value»; the ones that must
be secret and random (SECRET_KEY, DB_PASSWORD…), in «Generate on the
server»: they are created once and do not change.
Domain: with Caddy or nginx on the server, it is added to its sites by itself.
One app per template: for another one, attach another template to the same server.

variables.name: git_app_source
variables.label: Where the code comes from
variables.help: «git» = from a repository (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo…). «carpeta» = from a folder on this computer: Draupnode uploads it to the server every time you apply (no need to know git).

variables.name: git_app_local_dir
variables.label: Folder on this computer
variables.help: Only with «carpeta»: the project's, with its docker-compose (Docker Creator generates it). It is uploaded without .git, .env, virtual environments or node_modules (nor what its .dockerignore lists).

variables.name: git_app_repo
variables.label: Repository
variables.help: Only with «git»: https://github.com/user/repo.git (public, or private with the token below) or git@github.com:user/repo.git (private, with a deploy key).

variables.name: git_app_token
variables.label: Access token (only if the repository is private)
variables.help: For an https:// address of a private repository. On GitHub: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens, only this repository and «Contents: Read-only» permission (on GitLab/Forgejo, a token with repository read access). It is stored encrypted in your vault and is not left written on the server. If it is public, leave it empty. Without a token: use the git@… address and the deploy key.

variables.name: git_app_name
variables.label: App name
variables.help: For its folder and its containers.

variables.name: git_app_compose
variables.label: Compose file
variables.help: Inside the repository.

variables.name: git_app_env
variables.label: Variables (.env)
variables.help: Your app's non-secret ones, one per row (name and value). The highlighted ones must be completed or reviewed before applying. Passwords do not go here: in «Generate on the server (random secrets)» or in «Secret variables».

variables.name: git_app_env_generate
variables.label: Generate on the server (random secrets)
variables.help: Variable names, one per line (SECRET_KEY, DB_PASSWORD…). They are created once and kept. If the app requires a format, add it with «:»: NAME:fernet (cryptography.Fernet key), NAME:base64-32 (32 bytes in Base64), NAME:hex-32, NAME:hex-64 (e.g. Rails' SECRET_KEY_BASE), NAME:laravel (Laravel's APP_KEY, «base64:…»). With nothing: 40 letters and numbers.

variables.name: git_app_env_secret
variables.label: Secret variables with your own value
variables.help: Tokens or keys you already have: «KEY=value; OTHER=value». They are stored encrypted in your vault.

variables.name: git_app_post_command
variables.label: Command after starting
variables.help: It runs every time you apply, inside the service below, with the app already running. To prepare the database: «./manage.py migrate» (Django), «php artisan migrate --force» (Laravel), «npx prisma migrate deploy»… Empty = nothing.

variables.name: git_app_post_service
variables.label: Service where the command runs
variables.help: The service name in the docker-compose (e.g. web, app).
variables.patternHelp: Name of a service in the compose file

variables.name: git_app_owner
variables.label: Owner of the app folder
variables.help: If the app runs in the container with a non-root user and needs to write to its folder («Permission denied» error), put its UID:GID here, e.g. 1000:1000. Empty = leaves it as it is (root's).

variables.name: git_app_build_minutes
variables.label: Maximum build time (minutes)
variables.help: If the build takes longer, it is stopped. It is also stopped if it goes 10 minutes without progress (without writing anything).

variables.name: git_app_db
variables.label: Database
variables.help: «propia» = the one the docker-compose brings (or none). «postgres-compartido» = this server's shared PostgreSQL: Draupnode adds it if missing, creates a database and a user named after the app, connects the app to its network and passes it the details (DATABASE_URL, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_*, Laravel's DB_DATABASE/DB_USERNAME). The ones you set in «Variables (.env)» win.

variables.name: git_app_port
variables.label: App port on the server
variables.help: The one your compose file publishes (for the domain and the check). 0 = do not check.

variables.name: git_app_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: git_app_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual with a domain). Otherwise, it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: git_app_update
variables.label: Fetch the latest from Git when applying

secrets.label: Deploy key (add it to the repository, read-only)

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the app's containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its folder, its Docker volumes (the app's data and its database) and its generated values.

prueba.lab: Yes: it is exactly what the test server is for. Try it with a public repository or with a folder on your computer.
pasos: With a folder on your computer: in Docker Creator choose the folder, «Save to the folder» and «Publish on the server» with the test server; «Your app» ends up added with its variables (the «Publish your app step by step» guide tells it all).
With Git: add «Your app (Git or folder)» with «git» and a public repository, and press «Read the repository» to fill in its variables.
Check the highlighted variables and press «Simulate» (it checks the compose file, the variables and the ports without touching the app).
Press «Apply» and then «Open (SSH tunnel)».
comprobar: The app responds in the browser and, if it has a database, has run its migrations.
Server page → Apps and databases → Usage per app: it shows with its CPU and memory.
Change something in your project, apply again and it is updated.
necesita: Where the code comes from: «git» with the repository address (and a read-only token or a deploy key if it is private) or «carpeta» with the one on your computer. It must have a docker-compose.yml.
«App name» (its folder and its containers) and «App port on the server»: the one your compose file publishes on 127.0.0.1 (0 = do not check). Each app on the server, with a different name and port.

The variables of its .env («Read the repository» or Docker Creator fill them in); passwords, in «Generate on the server (random secrets)». If it uses a database, «postgres-compartido» or its own in the compose file.
problemas: «Permission denied» → the image does not run as root: put its UID:GID in «Owner of the app folder».
It responds but gives database errors → the database needs preparing: set «Command after starting» (./manage.py migrate, php artisan migrate --force…).
«port is already allocated» or the port in red → another app uses that port: change the one in the compose file and «App port on the server».
The build gets cut off → it takes longer than «Maximum build time (minutes)» or goes 10 minutes without writing anything (development or watch mode in the Dockerfile).
Below an app error, «What it means» appears with the most likely cause (a missing library, a variable, the database extension…).

name: nginx (web and proxy)
description: Publishes your apps on your domain with nginx, the most widely used web server. HTTPS with certbot (Let's Encrypt), which renews by itself.
details:
nginx (BSD-2) and certbot (Apache-2) from the Ubuntu/Debian repositories.
Each line in «Sites» is «domain target»:
  photos.example.com 127.0.0.1:2283      → forwards to the app on that port
  blog.example.com /srv/www/blog         → serves that folder (static website)
Each site goes in its own file /etc/nginx/sites-available/draupnode-<domain>.conf;
yours (the ones not starting with draupnode-) are not touched.
With HTTPS, certbot requests each domain's certificate and redirects http→https.
The domain must already point to this server's IP: if not, that site
stays on http and you are warned (applying again retries it).
Before reloading, the configuration is checked (nginx -t): if it fails, the
previous one is restored.
If you don't know which to choose, Caddy is simpler; nginx is the best known.
It cannot go with Coolify or Caddy: all three want ports 80 and 443.

variables.name: nginx_sites
variables.label: Sites
variables.help: One line per site: «domain target». Target = 127.0.0.1:PORT (an app) or /folder (static website).

variables.name: nginx_email
variables.label: Email for Let's Encrypt
variables.help: Required with HTTPS. They warn you if a certificate cannot be renewed.

variables.name: nginx_max_body_mb
variables.label: Maximum upload size (MB)
variables.help: What can be uploaded at once (photos, documents…).

variables.name: nginx_security_headers
variables.label: Security headers
variables.help: Not letting the website be framed by another, not guessing file types, not revealing the nginx version…

uninstallWarning: Uninstalls nginx and certbot. Your sites can no longer be seen through their domain; the apps behind keep running.
uninstallData: Also delete the Let's Encrypt certificates (/etc/letsencrypt) and the nginx configuration.

prueba.lab: Yes, but without certbot (the test server is not reachable from the internet): turn off HTTPS for the test. With a real domain it is tested on a public server.
pasos: First install something that listens, for example «Vaultwarden» (port 8222).
Add «nginx» with the site «vault.localhost 127.0.0.1:8222», HTTPS off, and apply.

In «Terminal»: «curl -s -H 'Host: vault.localhost' http://127.0.0.1 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}
'» and the same with another domain.
comprobar: With vault.localhost it returns 200; with a domain it does not know, nginx drops the connection (000).
«curl -sI -H 'Host: vault.localhost' http://127.0.0.1» does not show the nginx version and has the security headers.
necesita: The sites, one per line: «domain target» (127.0.0.1:PORT or /folder).
With HTTPS on, the email is required (certbot) and the domain must point to the server with 80 and 443 open.
problemas: certbot fails («Challenge failed», «DNS problem») → the domain does not point here yet or 80 is closed at the provider; to test without a domain, turn off HTTPS.
A domain not in the list does not respond → that is on purpose: nginx drops connections to domains it does not know.
Uploading large files gives «413» → raise «Maximum upload size (MB)».

name: Adminer (view and edit databases)
description: A page to view and edit your PostgreSQL and MariaDB databases: tables, data, SQL queries, import and export.
details:
Adminer (a single PHP file) in Docker, on the shared databases' network.
When you log in, choose the system and type the server
(«pg-compartido» or «mariadb-compartido», or your app's container
name) with its user and password (in «Passwords»).
It stores nothing. Better without a domain: log in with «Open» (SSH tunnel).
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/adminer (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: Apache-2.0 or GPL-2.0.

variables.name: adminer_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: adminer_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: adminer_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: adminer_network
variables.label: Docker network
variables.help: The same as the shared PostgreSQL/MariaDB («apps» if you have not changed it). The apps on that network reach this container by its name.
variables.patternHelp: Letters, numbers, dot, hyphen and underscore

variables.name: adminer_update
variables.label: Update Adminer when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Adminer containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (nothing (Adminer stores no data)). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes (with «Shared PostgreSQL» or «Shared MariaDB» so there is something to connect to).
pasos: Add «Shared PostgreSQL» and «Adminer», and apply.
Press «Open (SSH tunnel)» on Adminer and log in: system PostgreSQL, server «pg-compartido», user and password from «Passwords».
comprobar: It shows the databases and lets you open tables and run SQL queries.
necesita: Nothing in Adminer. To log in, the database user and password (in «Passwords»).
problemas: «No such host» when logging in → the database is not on the same Docker network: set your database's network in «Docker network» («apps» by default).

name: Shared MariaDB
description: A MariaDB (MySQL-compatible) in Docker for your apps, with one database and one user per app. The passwords are generated on the server.
details:
MariaDB (GPL-2) in Docker. It is only reachable from the given Docker network
(the apps see it by the container name); no port is published.
The passwords are generated on the server itself the first time and
stored in /etc/draupnode/secretos/<project>/ (root only); Draupnode brings
a copy to your vault. The Backups module dumps its databases every day.
It can go together with the shared PostgreSQL (each app uses the one it needs).

variables.name: mariadb_version
variables.label: MariaDB version
variables.help: The LTS ones (with years of updates).

variables.name: mariadb_container
variables.label: Container name
variables.help: It is the «host» your apps connect to.

variables.name: mariadb_databases
variables.label: Databases
variables.help: One per line. Each one will have a user with the same name and its own password.
variables.patternHelp: Lowercase letters, numbers and _ (starting with a letter)

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the MariaDB container. The apps that use it are left without a database.
uninstallData: Also delete the DATA of all databases and their passwords. This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «Shared MariaDB» with a database, for example «blog», and apply.
See its user and password on the module page → Passwords.
In «Terminal»: «docker exec -it mariadb-compartido mariadb -u blog -p blog -e 'select 1'» (paste the password).
comprobar: The query returns 1.
Server page → Apps and databases → Databases: MariaDB appears with the «blog» database.
necesita: The databases you want, one per line (lowercase letters, numbers and _). Each one with its user and password (in Passwords).
problemas: An app does not connect → it must be on the «apps» network and use the host mariadb-compartido.
«Access denied» with root → the root password is in Passwords (MariaDB «root» user).

name: Shared PostgreSQL
description: A PostgreSQL in Docker for all your apps, with one database and one user per app. The passwords are generated on the server.
details:
It is only reachable from the given Docker network (the apps see it by the container
name). The passwords are generated on the server itself the first
time and stored in /etc/draupnode/secretos/<project>/ (root only); they are never
overwritten when relaunching.

variables.name: postgres_container
variables.label: Container name
variables.help: It is the «host» your apps connect to.

variables.name: postgres_databases
variables.label: Databases
variables.help: One per line. Each one will have a user with the same name and its own password.
variables.patternHelp: Lowercase letters, numbers and _ (starting with a letter)

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the PostgreSQL container. The apps that use it are left without a database.
uninstallData: Also delete the DATA of all databases and their passwords. This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «Shared PostgreSQL» with a database, for example «tienda», and apply.
See the user and password of «tienda» on the module page → Passwords.
In «Terminal»: «docker exec -it pg-compartido psql -U tienda -d tienda -c 'select 1'».
comprobar: The query returns 1.
Server page → Apps and databases → Databases: pg-compartido appears with the «tienda» database and its size.
If you uninstall without «delete data» and install again, the database and its password are still there.
necesita: The databases you want, one per line (lowercase letters, numbers and _; starting with a letter). Each one will have a user with its name and its password (in Passwords).
problemas: An app does not connect → it must be on the «apps» network and use the host pg-compartido (with «Your app», choose «postgres-compartido» and it does it by itself).
You removed a database from the list and it is still there → databases are not deleted so as not to lose data; delete it by hand if you want.

name: Valkey (Redis-compatible cache)
description: In-memory cache and queues, Redis-compatible, for your apps. It is the free continuation of Redis (which stopped being free software in 7.4).
details:
Valkey 9 in Docker, shared by your apps: it listens on 127.0.0.1 and,
inside Docker, as «valkey-compartido» on the given network (the one of the
shared PostgreSQL and MariaDB). With a password (in «Passwords»).
In your apps: redis://:PASSWORD@valkey-compartido:6379/0
It stores the data on disk (appendonly) so it is not lost on restart.
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/valkey (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: BSD-3-Clause.

variables.name: valkey_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: valkey_network
variables.label: Docker network
variables.help: The same as the shared PostgreSQL/MariaDB («apps» if you have not changed it). The apps on that network reach this container by its name.
variables.patternHelp: Letters, numbers, dot, hyphen and underscore

variables.name: valkey_maxmemory_mb
variables.label: Maximum memory (MB)
variables.help: 0 = no limit. If it fills up, it deletes the least used keys (cache mode).

variables.name: valkey_update
variables.label: Update Valkey when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Valkey containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (what your apps store in Valkey). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «Valkey» and apply.
In «Terminal»: «sudo docker run --rm --network apps valkey/valkey:9 valkey-cli -h valkey-compartido -a PASSWORD ping» (the password is in «Passwords»).
comprobar: The test command answers «PONG»; without a password it answers «NOAUTH».
It only listens on 127.0.0.1:6379 and on the «apps» Docker network: it cannot be seen from outside.
necesita: Nothing. In your apps: redis://:PASSWORD@valkey-compartido:6379/0, connecting their container to the «apps» network.
problemas: Your app cannot find it → its container must be on the «apps» network (the same as «Docker network»).
Warning «Memory overcommit must be enabled» in its logs → it is only a warning; if you want to remove it: «vm.overcommit_memory = 1» in /etc/sysctl.d/.

name: Backup destination (rest-server)
description: Turns this server into the place where OTHER servers store their backups. It only lets backups be added, never deleted, so an intruder on the other server cannot destroy them.
details:
Uses rest-server (by the restic authors, BSD-2) in Docker, with HTTPS and
in «append-only» mode (--append-only): the source servers can
upload new backups but not delete or change the existing ones. Each source
server has its own user and folder and cannot see the others'
(--private-repos). Backups arrive encrypted: this server cannot
read them.
Normally you don't touch this by hand: on the page of another server's
«Backups» module, «Also store on another server…» creates this template and
leaves both sides configured (user, password and certificate).
Rotation: with «Delete old backups» on, THIS server deletes
every day the ones older than the given days (and keeps one a month if you
ask). For that it needs each server's backups password:
Draupnode gives it when applying (once it has it, that is, after
applying on the source server). That way this server could read the backups;
if you don't want that, turn it off and nothing will ever be deleted here (watch the
disk).

variables.name: backup_target_port
variables.label: HTTPS port
variables.help: The source servers connect through it. It is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: backup_target_dir
variables.label: Backups folder
variables.help: Inside, one folder per source server.

variables.name: backup_target_clients
variables.label: Servers that store here
variables.help: Draupnode fills them in («name:hash of its password»). Removing a line removes its access; its backups stay.

variables.name: backup_target_tls_cert
variables.label: HTTPS certificate
variables.help: Draupnode generates it (in base64). The source servers use it to check that they are talking to this one and not another.

variables.name: backup_target_tls_key
variables.label: HTTPS private key
variables.help: Draupnode generates it and it is stored encrypted in your vault.

variables.name: backup_target_prune
variables.label: Delete old backups (rotation)
variables.help: This server deletes every day the backups older than the days below. It needs the backups' password (Draupnode gives it when applying).

variables.name: backup_target_keep_days
variables.label: Keep the backups of the last (days)

variables.name: backup_target_keep_monthly
variables.label: And also one backup a month for (months)
variables.help: 0 = no more.

variables.name: backup_target_prune_time
variables.label: Rotation time
variables.help: Better far from the backup time (while it rotates, the source waits to back up).

uninstallWarning: Stops rest-server and the rotation. The other servers can no longer store their backups here (their remote backup will fail until you choose another destination).
uninstallData: Also delete ALL the backups stored here. If the source server is lost, there will be nothing to restore from.

prueba.lab: Two servers are needed: the test one as destination and another (a second Ubuntu, or a VPS) as source. With only one, just check that the destination starts.
pasos: It is not added by hand: on the source server (with «Backups»), Backups tab → «Also store on another server» and choose the destination.
Draupnode adds this module to the destination with its certificate and configures the source's backups; press «Apply both now».
On the source, «Back up now» and then «See remote backups».
comprobar: The source's backups appear on the destination.
The destination's backups cannot be deleted from the source (append-only mode): an intruder on the source cannot destroy them.
necesita: Nothing by hand: it is configured from the server that makes the backups (Backups → «Also store on another server»), which sets the certificate and passwords.
At least 10 GB free, and the port (8000 by default) open in the provider's firewall for the source server.
problemas: «HTTPS private key: Draupnode sets it…» in red → do not add it by hand, use «Also store on another server».
The source cannot reach it («connection refused», «timeout») → the port is closed at the destination's cloud provider.
The destination's IP changed → use «Also store on another server» again: the certificate is tied to the address.
It clashes with Coolify on 8000 → change the destination's port.

name: Backups (restic)
description: Daily encrypted backup with restic of your databases, Coolify, the secrets folder and the folders you choose. Optionally, a second copy outside the server.
details:
restic (open source, BSD) stores the backups encrypted and deduplicated in
{carpeta}/<project>/restic-repo. Its password is generated on the server and
Draupnode brings it to your vault: WITHOUT IT THE BACKUPS CANNOT BE OPENED.
Every day at the given time (systemd): it dumps PostgreSQL and the
Coolify database if present, copies Draupnode's secrets folder and your folders,
deletes old backups according to what you keep and checks the repository.
A backup that is only on the server does not save you if you lose the server:
use «Bring backups to this computer», or a remote destination of your own
(another server over SFTP, a restic rest-server or an S3-compatible store like
MinIO or Garage; all open source).

variables.name: backups_time
variables.label: Daily backup time
variables.help: Server time (HH:MM). It is delayed up to 10 minutes at random.

variables.name: backups_paths
variables.label: Folders to back up
variables.help: One per line. Draupnode's secrets folder is always backed up.

variables.name: backups_postgres
variables.label: Dump PostgreSQL
variables.help: All the databases of the given container (pg_dumpall), if it exists.

variables.name: backups_mariadb
variables.label: Dump MariaDB
variables.help: Each database of the given container (mariadb-dump), if it exists.

variables.name: backups_apps
variables.label: Back up Draupnode's apps
variables.help: The /srv/draupnode/apps folder (code, .env and data of the apps installed with Draupnode), if it exists.

variables.name: backups_coolify
variables.label: Back up Coolify
variables.help: Its database, its .env and its SSH keys, if Coolify is installed.

variables.name: backups_check
variables.label: Check the repository after each backup

variables.name: backups_run_now
variables.label: Make the first backup when applying

variables.name: backups_dir
variables.label: Backups folder on the server
variables.help: One folder per server is created inside.

variables.name: backups_remote_type
variables.label: Also back up outside the server
variables.help: «sftp» = another server of yours; «rest-server» = restic's backup server; «s3» = S3-compatible (MinIO, Garage…).

variables.name: backups_remote
variables.label: Remote destination
variables.help: sftp: user@203.0.113.40:/srv/copias/web · rest-server: https://backups.example.com:8000/web · s3: https://minio.example.com/bucket/web

variables.name: backups_remote_password
variables.label: Destination password (rest-server) or Secret Key (s3)
variables.help: It is stored encrypted in your vault and only travels to the server when applying.

variables.name: backups_remote_cacert
variables.label: Destination certificate (rest-server)
variables.help: Draupnode fills it in when the destination is another server of yours with the «Backup destination» module (its own certificate, in base64). Empty = normal certificate (Let's Encrypt…).

variables.name: backups_remote_append_only
variables.label: The destination is append-only
variables.help: Old backups on the destination are not deleted from here (the destination does not allow it). This server's are.

secrets.label: Public key for the backup server (SFTP)

uninstallWarning: Removes the daily backup (timer and script). Backups already made are kept.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: With «Shared PostgreSQL» installed, add «Backups» with «Make the first backup when applying» and apply.
Server page → Backups tab: press «See backups» and then «Back up now».
Try restoring: on a backup, «Restore database…» → «Restore into the new database» (not in its place).
comprobar: The backups appear with their date and size, and the dump of each database (postgres-…/tienda.dump).
The restored database has the same data as the original.
«Bring backups to this computer» downloads the backup to your computer.
necesita: Nothing for the daily local backup (databases, apps, Coolify and the secrets folder). Add yours in «Folders to back up» (absolute paths).
To also store outside: the type (sftp, rest-server or s3) and the address (e.g. sftp: user@203.0.113.40:/srv/copias/web). The easiest: «Also store on another server» from the Backups tab.
At least 5 GB free.
problemas: The remote SFTP backup fails with «Permission denied (publickey)» → add on the other server the public key shown in Passwords («Public key for the backup server (SFTP)»).
Alert «The last backup is more than 26 h old» → look at the backup log (Backups tab) and check that the server's clock is synchronised.
Without the backups password (restic) they cannot be restored: do «Export backup…» (Settings) in Draupnode and keep it off the computer.

name: Alerts to your phone
description: Warns you on your phone when something goes wrong (disk almost full, a backup that failed, a container down, another server not responding) and when it gets fixed.
details:
A small script on the server (systemd, every few minutes) checks what
you tick and sends the alert through ntfy (open source: the ntfy phone
app, with ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server) or Telegram.
It warns once when a problem starts, reminds you every few hours if it
continues, and warns when it is fixed.
With ntfy, if you leave the topic empty a long secret one is generated (whoever knows
the name can read the alerts). On this module's page you have the QR code
to subscribe from the app and a button to send a test alert.
A server cannot warn that it has gone down itself: for that, put its
address in «Watch other servers» in the alerts of ANOTHER server, or
tick «Daily notice»: if one day it does not arrive, something is wrong.

prueba.lab: Yes, with ntfy (no account): the alert reaches the phone even from the test server, because it is the server that calls ntfy.sh. Telegram needs a bot (@BotFather) and your chat id.
pasos: Add «Alerts to your phone» with the ntfy channel and apply.
On the module page: «Subscribe on your phone» (QR code for the ntfy app) and «Send a test alert».
Press «What it sees now». To force an alert, stop a container in the Containers tab and wait 5 minutes.
comprobar: The test alert reaches the phone.
«What it sees now» shows disk, memory, backups and containers with their status.
When you stop the container an alert arrives, and another when you start it again.
necesita: With ntfy: nothing (the secret topic is generated by itself). Then «Subscribe on your phone» with the ntfy app.
With Telegram: the bot token (@BotFather gives it to you) and your chat number (write to the bot and check it with @userinfobot).
Optional: disk and RAM thresholds, and other servers to watch («IP:port», one per line).
problemas: Nothing arrives → press «Send a test alert»; if that does not arrive either, the server cannot reach the internet or the topic/token is wrong.
Nothing arrives on Telegram → first send /start to your bot (bots cannot write to someone who has not talked to them).
Repeated alerts arrive → they repeat every «Remind about an ongoing problem every (hours)» while it is still wrong; raise it if it bothers you.

Draupnode creates the key the hub uses to talk to agents and the
administrator user (email admin@beszel.local, password in

a shared socket, without opening any port. To watch other servers,
install the Beszel agent on them with the same key (the public one,
which you see when you press “Add system”).
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/beszel (included in the backups of the
Backups module). License: MIT.

details:
Cockpit (LGPL-2.1) from the system. It is not published on the internet: it only listens
on 127.0.0.1 (and on the VPN if WireGuard is there). It opens with «Open» on this
module's page (SSH tunnel), through the VPN or with a domain (Caddy or nginx
on the server).
To log in, Draupnode creates its own user with a password generated
on the server (in «Passwords»); if you tick «Can
administer», that user has sudo.

pasos: Add «Cockpit» and apply.
Press «Open (SSH tunnel)» and log in with the user from Passwords.
comprobar: The panel shows CPU, memory, services and logs, and its terminal works.
It only listens on 127.0.0.1 (and on the VPN if there is one): it cannot be seen from outside.

Dozzle in Docker. It only reads: it stores nothing and does not touch the containers.
It asks for a user and password («admin», password in «Passwords»):

To keep the logs and search them days later, the «Logs» module

name: Healthchecks (did my tasks run?)
description: Warns you when a scheduled task does NOT run: backups, cron, scripts. Each task pings an address when it finishes; if one day it does not arrive, you find out.
details:
Healthchecks in Docker, with its SQLite database. Draupnode creates the
administrator user (email admin@localhost, password in «Passwords»).
Create one check per task and add at the end of the task:
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 5 https://your-domain/ping/<code>
Better on a server DIFFERENT from the tasks' one, and with a domain so
that pings from other servers arrive.
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/healthchecks (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: BSD-3-Clause.

name: Logs (Loki)
description: Stores and searches in Grafana the logs of all containers and of the system (SSH, sudo, services). Loki + Grafana Alloy.
details:
Loki stores the logs and Grafana Alloy collects them: the output of each
Docker container and the system journal (journald). They are searched in Grafana,
in the «Container logs» dashboard. All open source.
It needs Monitoring (it uses its Grafana). It takes about 300-500 MB of RAM;
that is why it is separate.

variables.name: logs_journal
variables.label: System logs (journald)
variables.help: SSH, sudo, services, backups… on top of the containers.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes Loki and Alloy, and the Grafana logs dashboard.
uninstallData: Also delete the stored logs.

prueba.lab: Yes (it needs Monitoring and 2 GB of RAM).
pasos: With Monitoring installed, add «Logs (Loki)» and apply.
In Grafana, open the «Logs» dashboard or Explore → Loki.
In «Terminal», do something that leaves a trace (for example «sudo true» or restarting a container).
comprobar: The logs of the containers and the system (SSH, sudo, services) appear, and what you did shows up straight away.
necesita: Nothing (it needs Monitoring). 2 GB of RAM; it keeps 14 days by default.
problemas: No system logs appear → turn on «System logs (journald)».
The disk fills up → lower «Days of logs to keep».

name: Monitoring (metrics)
description: Prometheus and Grafana with ready-made dashboards for the server's CPU, RAM and disk, each container and PostgreSQL. Grafana opens from Draupnode through an SSH tunnel.
details:
All in Docker and open source: Prometheus, node-exporter (the server),
cAdvisor (each container), postgres-exporter (if there is PostgreSQL in this
same template) and Grafana OSS with the «Resources» and «PostgreSQL» dashboards.
Grafana and Prometheus only listen on the server itself (127.0.0.1): they are not
opened to the internet or in the Firewall. Draupnode opens them through the same
SSH connection («Open Grafana» on the module page). The user is admin;
the password is generated on the server and you have it in its passwords.
It takes about 400-600 MB of RAM.

variables.help: CPU and RAM per container. It needs Docker's classic storage (option of the Docker module).

variables.name: monitoring_postgres

variables.help: Only if PostgreSQL is in this same template (it uses its superuser password).

variables.help: Local only. Draupnode uses it for the summary on the module page.

pasos: Add «Monitoring (metrics)» and apply.

«Open Grafana» does not load → the SSH tunnel needs the connection password stored or the vault open.

name: AdGuard Home (no ads on the VPN)

details:
AdGuard Home (GPL-3) in Docker. Its DNS only listens on the VPN (WireGuard's .1),
never on the internet: an open DNS is used to attack others.
Draupnode sets its address as the DNS of the VPN devices (you have to
scan the QR code again or import their .conf).
Its panel can only be seen from the server: «Open» on the module page
(SSH tunnel), through the VPN or with a domain. User and password generated on
the server (in «Passwords»).
Queries go out encrypted (DNS over HTTPS) to Quad9 and Cloudflare;
you can change that in its panel.

Press «Open (SSH tunnel)» and log in with the user from Passwords.

The AdGuard panel loads and counts the queries; the WireGuard configurations have DNS = 10.8.0.1.

problemas: It does not block ads → the device is not using the VPN, or its configuration predates AdGuard: import the one from «See configurations» again (it has DNS = 10.8.0.1).
A legitimate website does not load → add it to the allowlist in the AdGuard panel.

details:

gives you (Site administration → Actions → Runners → “Create new
runner”, or in a repository/organization settings) and runs each job
in a new container, with the labels you set (by default, ubuntu-latest
= node:20-bookworm, which understands most GitHub actions).

root: use it only with trusted repositories, ideally on a separate
server. Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/forgejo-runner.

details:

(wg0, if WireGuard is there) and on the local network interfaces you specify
(for example eth0 on a home Raspberry Pi). It opens nothing in the
Firewall: sharing files over the internet without a VPN is dangerous.
Each line in «Folders» is «name /path»; you log in with the module's user
and its password generated on the server (in «Passwords»). From the VPN: \\10.8.0.1\name (Windows) or
smb://10.8.0.1/name (macOS/Linux).

variables.label: Folders
variables.help: One per line: «name /path» (e.g. «documents /srv/compartido/documentos»). They are created if they do not exist.

variables.label: Local network interfaces
variables.help: Besides the VPN. Empty = VPN only. Example: eth0 (see «ip a» on the server).

uninstallData: Also delete the Samba user (the folders and their files are NOT deleted).

prueba.lab: Yes (it needs WireGuard, or a network interface in «Local network interfaces»).
pasos: With WireGuard installed, add «Samba» with the folder «compartido /srv/compartido» and apply.
In «Terminal»: «sudo apt-get install -y smbclient» and «smbclient //10.8.0.1/compartido -U compartir» (password from Passwords); inside, «put /etc/hostname prueba.txt» and «ls».
comprobar: It uploads and lists the file; with another user it gives LOGON_FAILURE.
It listens on 10.8.0.1 and 127.0.0.1, never on the public IP.
necesita: The folders, one per line: «name /path» (created if they do not exist). The user and its password are in Passwords.
WireGuard (it only listens on the VPN) or a local network interface in «Local network interfaces» (e.g. eth0). It is never opened to the internet.
problemas: The folder cannot be seen → connect to the VPN first and use \\10.8.0.1\name (Windows) or smb://10.8.0.1/name (macOS/Linux).
«LOGON_FAILURE» → user or password: use the ones from Passwords.
You cannot write → the folder on the server belongs to another user; the one Draupnode creates does allow it.

name: Stalwart (complete mail server)
description: Your own mail server: receives and sends (SMTP), mailboxes (IMAP and JMAP), filters and anti-spam, all in one, with a web page to manage it.
details:

firewall. The “admin” user of the administration web page and its
password (temporary, to get started) are created by Stalwart the first
time; Draupnode copies them to “Passwords”.
CAREFUL, your own email is demanding: you need a domain with its MX,
SPF, DKIM and DMARC records (Stalwart tells you which ones in
“Management → Domains → DNS records”), a provider that lets port 25
out (many block it: Hetzner and DigitalOcean open it if you ask) and
the IP's reverse DNS set to your domain.
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/stalwart (included in the backups of the
Backups module). License: AGPL-3.0.

name: AIDE (watch system files)
description: Keeps a «snapshot» of the important system files (programs, configuration) and every day tells you whether any has changed without you doing it.
details:
AIDE (GPL-2.0), Debian/Ubuntu's file integrity monitor.
When applying it takes the snapshot (the first time takes a few minutes). Every day
it compares it and leaves the result in /var/log/aide/aide.log.
Changes you make with Draupnode should not show up: with «Take
the snapshot when applying», the snapshot is redone after every apply.
It does not watch what changes by itself: app data, Docker, logs.
After updating the system you will see changes in programs: that is normal.

variables.name: aide_rebase_on_apply
variables.label: Take the snapshot when applying
variables.help: After applying (changes you have made) it redoes the snapshot, so it only warns you about what you did not do.

variables.name: aide_exclude
variables.label: Folders that are not watched
variables.help: Besides the default ones (app data, Docker, logs). One per line.

uninstallWarning: Removes AIDE and its daily check.
uninstallData: Also delete the stored snapshot and the logs.

prueba.lab: Yes (the first snapshot takes a few minutes).
pasos: Add «AIDE» and apply.
In «Terminal», change a watched file: «echo '# prueba' | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts» and run the check: «sudo systemctl start dailyaidecheck».
comprobar: «ls -lh /var/lib/aide/aide.db» exists.
After the test, «sudo tail -n 40 /var/log/aide/aide.log» shows /etc/hosts as changed. If you apply AIDE again, it stops showing (new snapshot).
necesita: Nothing. Optional: folders of yours that change by themselves and you don't want watched.
problemas: It warns about many changes after updating the system → that is normal: apply AIDE again to take the new snapshot.

Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/authelia (included in the backups of the
