name: ClamAV (antivirus)
description: Scans for viruses and malware every night in the folders you choose (for example, what users upload to your apps), with the signature database always up to date.
details:
ClamAV (GPL-2.0), Cisco Talos's free antivirus. freshclam
updates the signatures several times a day; the scan is a separate
command, at the given time and with low priority so it does not get in the way.
It only warns: it does not delete or move anything. What it finds is left in
/var/lib/draupnode/clamav/encontrado.txt and in the scan note.
During the scan it uses ~1.5 GB of RAM (it loads all the signatures).

variables.name: clamav_paths
variables.label: Folders to scan
variables.help: One per line. The ones with your apps' data and the users' ones. Do not put the whole «/» (it would take hours).

uninstallWarning: Removes ClamAV and its daily scan.
uninstallData: Also delete the signature database (~300 MB) and the reports.

prueba.lab: Yes, if the test server has 2 GB free. The first signature download (~300 MB) takes a few minutes.
pasos: Add «ClamAV» with the default folders and apply.

In «Terminal», leave the EICAR test file (harmless): «echo 'X5O!P%@AP[4\PZX54(P^)7CC)7}$EICAR-STANDARD-ANTIVIRUS-TEST-FILE!$H+H*' | sudo tee /srv/eicar.txt» and run «sudo systemctl start draupnode-clamav».
comprobar: «systemctl status clamav-freshclam» is active and «ls /var/lib/clamav» has main, daily and bytecode.
After the test, «sudo cat /var/lib/draupnode/clamav/encontrado.txt» lists /srv/eicar.txt (delete it afterwards).
necesita: The folders to scan (the default ones will do) and the time.
problemas: The scan fails for lack of memory → the server needs 2 GB of RAM; add «Swap memory» or remove the module.
freshclam does not download («403» or «cool-down») → your provider's network is blocked by the signature server: wait a few hours.

name: CrowdSec (attack blocking)
description: Reads the server's logs, detects attacks (SSH brute force, scans, bots against your websites) and blocks those IPs in the firewall. It also uses the list of malicious IPs shared by the community.
details:
CrowdSec (MIT) from its official repository, with the iptables
bouncer. It watches SSH and the system, and nginx or Caddy if present. If there is
Docker, it also protects the ports the containers publish.
Your IP (the one you apply from) and the ones in «IPs that are never blocked» are
never blocked.
It can go together with fail2ban (Secure SSH module): they complement each other.
«Community list»: CrowdSec sends the IPs that attack you (nothing else)
and in return receives the ones attacking everyone.
Queries in the Terminal: sudo cscli decisions list (blocked IPs),
sudo cscli alerts list, sudo cscli metrics.

variables.name: crowdsec_whitelist
variables.label: IPs that are never blocked
variables.help: One IP or network per line (203.0.113.10 or 203.0.113.0/24). Your IP when applying is added by itself.

variables.name: crowdsec_community
variables.label: Community list
variables.help: Shares the IPs that attack you and receives the ones attacking others (free). Without this, it only blocks what it sees on this server.

uninstallWarning: Removes CrowdSec and its bouncer; the IPs it had blocked can get in again.
uninstallData: Also delete its configuration and its alerts database.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «CrowdSec» and apply.
In «Terminal», simulate an attack: «sudo cscli decisions add --ip 203.0.113.50 --duration 5m».
comprobar: «sudo cscli metrics» shows that it reads the SSH log (auth.log or journald) and «sudo cscli bouncers list» has the iptables bouncer.
After the test, «sudo cscli decisions list» shows 203.0.113.50 and «sudo iptables -S | grep -i crowdsec» has its rules; «sudo cscli decisions delete --ip 203.0.113.50» removes it.
Your own connection keeps working (your IP is on the allowlist).
necesita: Nothing. Optional: the IPs you always log in from (your home, your office, the VPN) in «IPs that are never blocked».
problemas: You have locked yourself out → log in through the provider's console and run «sudo cscli decisions delete --ip YOUR_IP»; then add your IP to the allowlist.
It does not watch nginx/Caddy → install those modules first and apply CrowdSec again (it detects what is there when applying).

name: Keycloak (single sign-on)
description: A single user and password (with two-factor) for all your apps: single sign-on with OpenID Connect and SAML, like «Sign in with Google» but yours.
details:
Keycloak 26 in Docker, with its own PostgreSQL. Draupnode creates the
temporary administrator «admin» (in «Passwords»): log in, create your
own administrator user in the «master» realm and delete «admin»
(Keycloak reminds you).
For your apps to use it, it needs a domain with HTTPS (Caddy or nginx).
It is heavy: it asks for 1.2 GB of RAM and takes a minute to start.
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/keycloak (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: Apache-2.0.

variables.name: keycloak_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: keycloak_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: keycloak_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: keycloak_update
variables.label: Update Keycloak when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the Keycloak containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (users, realms, clients and its database). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes, if the test server has 1.5 GB free (it takes a minute to start).
pasos: Add «Keycloak» and apply.
Press «Open (SSH tunnel)», log in to the console with «admin» and the password from «Passwords», and create a realm and a user.
comprobar: The administration console opens and lets you create realms, users and clients.

In «Terminal», the token answers 200: «curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -d grant_type=password -d client_id=admin-cli -d username=admin -d password=PASSWORD http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token».
necesita: Nothing to test it. For your apps to use it, a domain with Caddy or nginx.
problemas: It warns that «admin» is temporary → that is expected: create your own administrator in the master realm and delete «admin».
Apps say «invalid redirect_uri» or «HTTPS required» → give it a domain with HTTPS and use that address in the clients.

name: Lynis (security review)
description: Reviews the server's security (hundreds of checks) and gives you a score from 0 to 100 with specific advice to improve it. Every week, by itself.
details:
Lynis (GPL-3.0) by CISOfy, the leading free security auditor.
It only looks: it changes nothing. When applying it runs a review (1-2 minutes)
and, if you want, another one every week.
The report is left in /var/lib/draupnode/lynis/informe.txt; the advice
(«Suggestions») and warnings («Warnings») are what to look at.
Much of the advice is solved by other modules: Secure SSH, Firewall,
Automatic updates, auditd, AIDE…

variables.name: lynis_weekly
variables.label: Review every week
variables.help: Sundays in the early hours. The last review's report stays on the server.

variables.name: lynis_run_now
variables.label: Review when applying
variables.help: It takes 1-2 minutes. That way you see the score in the apply note.

uninstallWarning: Removes Lynis and its weekly review.
uninstallData: Also delete the stored reports.

prueba.lab: Yes (the score comes out lower than on a real server: a container has no kernel of its own).
pasos: Add «Lynis» with «Review when applying» and apply.
Then add «Secure SSH» or «Automatic updates», apply and apply Lynis again.
comprobar: The apply note says «Hardening index: N/100» and how many warnings and suggestions there are.
In «Terminal»: «sudo less /var/lib/draupnode/lynis/informe.txt» has the report and «systemctl list-timers draupnode-lynis.timer» the next review.
After adding other security modules, the score goes up.
necesita: Nothing.
problemas: The score looks low → that is normal the first time: look at the advice, much of it is fixed with other Security modules. There is no need to reach 100.

name: OpenBao (secrets vault)
description: Stores and hands out your apps' passwords, keys and certificates securely, with permissions and a log of who reads what. The free continuation of HashiCorp Vault.
details:
OpenBao 2 in Docker (Vault stopped being free software in 2023).
Draupnode initialises it the first time with a single unseal key and
stores the key and the root token in «Passwords»: COPY THEM to your password
manager; without the key, the data cannot be recovered.
When it restarts, OpenBao starts sealed. With «Unseal by itself»,
the server unseals it at startup using the key stored on it
(convenient, but anyone who gets root on the server can read everything).
Web panel at /ui (log in with the root token).
Its data is in /srv/draupnode/apps/openbao (included in the backups of the
Backups module). Licence: MPL-2.0.

variables.name: openbao_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The app listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: openbao_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: openbao_public_port
variables.label: Open a port to the internet
variables.help: 0 = no (the usual, with a domain or through the VPN). Otherwise http://IP:port and it is opened in the Firewall.

variables.name: openbao_auto_unseal
variables.label: Unseal by itself
variables.help: When the server starts (and when applying) it unseals it with the key stored on the server. Without this, you unseal it yourself in /ui with the key.

variables.name: openbao_update
variables.label: Update OpenBao when applying
variables.help: Downloads the latest version of the image every time you apply.

secrets.label: OpenBao unseal key and root token

uninstallWarning: Stops and removes the OpenBao containers.
uninstallData: Also delete its data (all the stored secrets (encrypted)). This cannot be undone.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «OpenBao» (with «Unseal by itself») and apply.
In «Terminal»: «sudo docker restart dn-openbao» and then «sudo systemctl start draupnode-openbao» (the same it does when the server starts).
comprobar: «Passwords» has the unseal key and the root token; with «Open (SSH tunnel)», /ui lets you log in with the token.
After restarting the container it is sealed («curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/seal-status» says sealed true) and the service unseals it.
necesita: Nothing. Copy the unseal key and the root token to your password manager.
problemas: After restarting the server it is sealed → without «Unseal by itself» you have to unseal it by hand in /ui with the key.
You have lost the unseal key → the data cannot be recovered: that is why you must copy it off the server.

name: Trivy (vulnerabilities in your containers)
description: Every week it reviews the images of the containers you have running and tells you which have known security flaws (CVE) and whether there is already a fixed version.
details:
Trivy (Apache-2.0) by Aqua Security, from its official repository.
It reviews the images of all running containers (including
Coolify's and your apps'). It only reports: updating is up to you (in each app,
«Update when applying» and apply; in yours, rebuild the image).
The report is left in /var/lib/draupnode/trivy/informe.txt.
The first time it downloads its vulnerability database (~1 GB on disk).

variables.name: trivy_severity
variables.label: Minimum severity
variables.help: Which flaws are counted. With «CRITICAL» only the most serious ones.

variables.name: trivy_ignore_unfixed
variables.label: Only the ones that already have a fix
variables.help: Hides the flaws for which there is no fixed version yet (you can't do anything about them).

variables.name: trivy_run_now
variables.label: Review when applying
variables.help: The first time takes several minutes (it downloads the vulnerability database).

uninstallWarning: Removes Trivy and its weekly review.
uninstallData: Also delete its vulnerability database (~1 GB) and the reports.

prueba.lab: Yes (with some container running, for example a catalog app).
pasos: Add an app (for example «Uptime Kuma») and «Trivy» with «Review when applying», and apply.
Change the severity to «CRITICAL» and apply again.
comprobar: The apply note says how many images it reviewed and how many flaws there are per image.
In «Terminal»: «sudo less /var/lib/draupnode/trivy/informe.txt» has the table of flaws and «systemctl list-timers draupnode-trivy.timer» the next review.
necesita: Nothing: the defaults (high and critical, only with a fix) are what is useful.
problemas: It fails downloading the database («TOOMANYREQUESTS» from ghcr.io) → wait a while and apply again.
Lots of flaws show up → update the apps (in each one, «Update when applying») and review again.

name: auditd (audit log)
description: Records who touches the important parts of the server (users, sudo, SSH, the clock, kernel modules, Docker) so you can investigate afterwards if something happens.
details:
The Linux kernel audit system (auditd, GPL-2.0) with a
sensible rule set for a server: changes to users and
passwords, sudoers, SSH configuration, cron, system time,
kernel modules and Docker, and every use of sudo.
Search in the Terminal: sudo ausearch -k draupnode-usuarios -i
(keys: draupnode-usuarios, -sudo, -ssh, -cron, -hora, -modulos,
-docker) or a summary with sudo aureport --summary.
With «Lock the rules» nobody (not even root) can change them without
restarting: safer, but to remove the module you have to restart.

variables.name: auditd_immutable
variables.label: Lock the rules
variables.help: Nobody can change them or turn off auditing without restarting the server.

variables.name: auditd_log_mb
variables.label: Size of each log (MB)
variables.help: 5 are kept; when full, they rotate.

uninstallWarning: Removes auditd and its rules. If the rules were locked, they are fully removed on restart.
uninstallData: Also delete the audit logs (/var/log/audit).

prueba.lab: No: a container cannot use kernel auditing. Try it on a virtual machine or a server.
pasos: Add «auditd» and apply.
In «Terminal», do something watched: «sudo useradd prueba-audit && sudo userdel prueba-audit».
comprobar: «sudo auditctl -l» shows the rules with the draupnode-… keys
«sudo ausearch -k draupnode-usuarios -i | tail» shows the test user being added and removed.
necesita: Nothing.
problemas: It fails loading the rules («Operation not permitted») → they were locked: restart the server and apply again.
It fails in a container or on old VPSs (OpenVZ/LXC) → there is no kernel auditing there: remove the module.

name: Argo CD (continuous deployment on Kubernetes)
description: GitOps: you tell it which Git repository describes your Kubernetes applications and Argo CD keeps the cluster the same as the repository, with a panel to see everything.
details:
Argo CD (Apache-2.0, CNCF) with its official installation in the
«argocd» namespace of this server's Kubernetes (k3s module).
The panel opens with «Open» (SSH tunnel), through the VPN or with a domain
(Caddy or nginx): a service on the server leaves it on 127.0.0.1.
User «admin»; its initial password is in «Passwords».
It needs ~1 GB of RAM on top of k3s.

variables.name: argocd_port
variables.label: Port on the server (local only)
variables.help: The panel listens on 127.0.0.1 on this port. It is reached through the domain (Caddy/nginx), through the VPN or with «Open» (SSH tunnel).

variables.name: argocd_domain
variables.label: Domain
variables.help: Optional. With Caddy or nginx on the server, it is published at https://domain.

variables.name: argocd_version
variables.label: Version
variables.help: «stable» = the latest stable. Or a specific one, like v3.2.0.

uninstallWarning: Removes Argo CD from the cluster. The applications it deployed stay in Kubernetes (no longer watched).

prueba.lab: Yes, if the test server has 3 GB of free RAM (k3s + Argo CD).
pasos: Add «Argo CD» (it adds k3s by itself) and apply; it takes a few minutes.

Press «Open (SSH tunnel)», log in with «admin» and create an example application: repository https://github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps.git, path «guestbook», cluster «in-cluster», namespace «default».
comprobar: The panel opens and lets you log in with the password from «Passwords».
The «guestbook» application reaches «Synced» and «Healthy», and «kubectl get pods» shows its pods.
necesita: Nothing: it installs with the defaults. Optional domain (with Caddy or nginx).
problemas: The panel does not open → look at «systemctl status draupnode-argocd» (the service that leaves it on 127.0.0.1) and «kubectl -n argocd get pods».
It runs out of memory → the server needs about 3 GB: add «Swap memory» or use a bigger one.

name: Kubernetes (k3s)
description: Full, lightweight Kubernetes on your server (k3s, CNCF-certified), with Helm to install Kubernetes applications with one command.
details:
k3s (Apache-2.0) by SUSE/Rancher: a single-binary Kubernetes,
designed for small servers (it asks for ~1 GB of RAM). It installs with its
official installer and its configuration in /etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml.
By default WITHOUT its Traefik or its load balancer, so they don't take
ports 80/443 from Caddy, nginx or Coolify: publish your services with a
domain in Caddy/nginx pointing to a NodePort, or turn on Traefik if the
server is only for Kubernetes.
Helm (Apache-2.0) is installed from get.helm.sh checking its SHA-256 sum.
In the Terminal: kubectl get pods -A (with sudo, or as your user if
you tick «kubectl for your user»).
It can go together with Docker: each one has its own containers.

variables.name: k3s_channel
variables.label: Version
variables.help: «stable» = the one k3s recommends. «latest» = the newest.

variables.name: k3s_update
variables.label: Update k3s when applying
variables.help: Runs the official installer again, which takes it to the latest version of the chosen channel.

variables.name: k3s_traefik
variables.label: Use k3s's Traefik and load balancer
variables.help: They take ports 80 and 443. Only if the server is only for Kubernetes (not with Caddy, nginx or Coolify).

variables.name: k3s_public_api
variables.label: Open the API (6443) to the internet
variables.help: To use kubectl from your computer without a tunnel. Better not: use the VPN or an SSH tunnel (ssh -L 6443:127.0.0.1:6443).

variables.name: k3s_user_kubeconfig
variables.label: kubectl for your user
variables.help: Copies cluster access to your SSH user's ~/.kube/config (if not root), to use kubectl without sudo.

uninstallWarning: Uninstalls k3s with its own uninstaller. EVERYTHING in the cluster IS DELETED (pods, volumes, secrets). Helm and your kubeconfig are removed too.

prueba.lab: Yes. If the test server was created before 0.63 it is very slow (k3s copies each whole image): delete it and create it again so it has its volume for Kubernetes.
pasos: Add «Kubernetes (k3s)» with Helm and apply (about 2 minutes).
In «Terminal»: «kubectl create deployment hola --image=nginx --port=80» and, after a while, «kubectl get pods».
comprobar: The apply note says the node is «Ready» with its version.
«kubectl get nodes» and «kubectl get pods -A» work as your user (without sudo) and «helm version» responds.
The «hola-…» pod reaches «Running» (delete it with «kubectl delete deployment hola»).
necesita: Nothing: the defaults (no Traefik, closed API, with Helm) work alongside Caddy, nginx or Coolify.
problemas: Pods cannot reach other services or the API (CrashLoop in coredns) → the firewall blocks the pod network: apply k3s again, which opens cni0 and the 10.42/10.43 networks.
Traefik does not start → ports 80/443 are taken by Caddy, nginx or Coolify: turn off «Use Traefik».

name: OpenTofu (infrastructure as code)
description: The free alternative to Terraform. Describe your infrastructure in files (DNS, cloud servers, buckets, accounts…) and OpenTofu creates it and keeps it that way. It reads the same .tf files.
details:
OpenTofu (MPL-2.0, Linux Foundation) from its official repository.
Terraform stopped being free software in 2023 (BUSL licence); OpenTofu
is its free continuation and uses the same files and providers.
It only installs the «tofu» command, or also, with a Git repository, prepares
a working folder: when applying it fetches the code, runs «tofu init» and
«tofu plan» and shows you the plan summary. With «Apply the plan» it
runs it («tofu apply»); otherwise, you apply it yourself in the Terminal.
The state (terraform.tfstate) is left in /srv/draupnode/apps/opentofu and
is included in the backups of the Backups module.
The providers' keys (your DNS API, your cloud's…) go in
«Secret variables»: they are stored encrypted in your vault.

variables.name: opentofu_repo
variables.label: Git repository with your .tf files
variables.help: Optional. https://… (public or with a token), or file:///path for a Git folder on the server itself. Empty = only installs «tofu».

variables.name: opentofu_token
variables.label: Access token (private repository)
variables.help: For a private repository over https (with read-only permission). Empty if it is public.

variables.name: opentofu_subdir
variables.label: Folder inside the repository
variables.help: Where the .tf files are. Empty = the root.

variables.name: opentofu_env
variables.label: Secret variables
variables.help: The ones your providers ask for, separated by «;»: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=xxx; TF_VAR_key=yyy

variables.name: opentofu_apply
variables.label: Apply the plan
variables.help: Besides planning, runs «tofu apply» (creates, changes or DELETES whatever the plan says). Check the plan first with this unticked.

uninstallWarning: Removes the «tofu» command. The infrastructure it created is NOT deleted (for that, «tofu destroy» first).
uninstallData: Also delete the working folder with the state (terraform.tfstate). Without the state, OpenTofu no longer knows what it created.

prueba.lab: Yes.
pasos: Add «OpenTofu» without a repository and apply: it only installs «tofu».

In «Terminal» create a test repository: «sudo mkdir -p /srv/tf && cd /srv/tf && sudo git init -q -b main && echo 'resource "terraform_data" "hola" { input = "mundo" }' | sudo tee main.tf && sudo git add . && sudo git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=prueba commit -qm uno». Set «file:///srv/tf» as the repository and apply; then tick «Apply the plan» and apply again.
comprobar: «tofu version» responds in the Terminal.
The first apply with a repository says «Plan: 1 to add»; with «Apply the plan», «Apply complete! Resources: 1 added», and the next one «No changes».
The state is in /srv/draupnode/apps/opentofu/trabajo (terraform.tfstate).
necesita: Nothing to have just «tofu». For the working folder: the repository with your .tf files and, if your providers ask for them, their keys in «Secret variables».
problemas: «tofu init» fails downloading a provider → the OpenTofu registry (registry.opentofu.org) does not respond or the provider does not exist with that name: check the required_providers block.
The plan asks for variables → set them as TF_VAR_name=value in «Secret variables», or with a default value in your .tf files.
